long_biography.plain_text:
Landscape restoration has linked Maria Iris Bertarelli’s work in Tuscany across farming, architecture and hospitality. At ColleMassari, she and Claudio Tipa restored historic farmhouses at Montecucco as agriturismo accommodation beside the vineyards. The wider estate combines organically farmed vines, olive groves and woodland, with contemporary agricultural design intended to protect the land’s character.

Bertarelli has also turned that local focus into cultural institutions. She co-founded Fondazione Bertarelli in 2009 and serves as its president, supporting art, archaeology, environmental restoration, architecture and music in Grosseto and wider Tuscany. Its projects have included the Amiata Piano Festival, the redevelopment of Poggi del Sasso’s historic centre and archaeological research with the University of Siena.
